ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Mahatma Gandhi

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Gandhi returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit, two months after his last review. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. His home blood pressure averages 126/72 on amlodipine 5 mg, and he has had no lightheadedness since the hot spell in June. He walks 5 km every morning, drinks more water in the heat, and has kept his weight at about 46 kg. He takes vitamin B12 and D daily. He has had no falls, emergency visits, or hospital stays. He has no fast planned at present and has agreed to tell the clinic before any future fast so the safety plan can be repeated. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He wants to be told the full truth about his health and to make his own decisions, including decisions about food and fasting. He accepts hospital care for illness that can be reversed. He would not want resuscitation, a breathing machine, or tube feeding if he could not recover the ability to walk and to think clearly. He has named a health care agent from his community and will put his wishes in writing; a copy will be scanned into the chart. [S]
